articles.title: Coke Plus is the fibermaxxing soda that Americans haven’t caught on to yet
articles.summary: On a recent trip to Japan, I found a fiber-forward soda that tastes like Diet Coke and keeps things moving. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: On my recent vacation to Japan, I learned they are light-years ahead of the US in many ways – from their high-tech toilets and efficient bullet trains to … diet sodas.

Amidst the chilled bottles of Coke Zero and Sugar-Free Pepsi stocked in the fridge of practically every 7-Eleven was another mysterious beverage in a bright white can – Coke Plus, which my friend heard about from the internet’s goldmine of travel videos.

Unlike Coca-Cola’s other diet sodas, Coke Plus has 5g of indigestible dextrin fiber, which it says can “suppress the absorption of fat from food and moderate neutral fat level spikes in the blood after eating”. Its target market? Adults 40 and up.

Coke Plus was ahead of its time. It debuted in Japan in 2017, before the fibermaxxing craze came to the US. Its launch attracted national attention, earning coverage in outlets such as New York Magazine and Business Insider. Despite the buzz, it never enjoyed a wide US release. Japan’s demographic skews older – over a quarter of its residents are at least 65 years old – which may, in part, explain its popularity.
points: On a recent trip to Japan, I found a fiber-forward soda that tastes like Diet Coke and keeps things moving.

articles.title: The pain of letting go of a loved one’s belongings | Letters
articles.summary: Readers respond to Polly Hudson’s article about disposing of her late mother’s possessions. Reading Polly Hudson’s account of clearing her mother’s house ( My mum has died – and every decision I make about her belongings feels wrong, 20 September ) made me think about my experience of doing the…
body: I was determined to recycle as much as possible, feeding the good things through to charity shops and going back later to see what had and hadn’t sold. When one charity shop in the Welsh border town where my mother lived didn’t want her manual typewriter, on the grounds that nobody would have use for it, I took it to a charity shop in London, which snapped it up and put it in the window.

Polly Hudson’s final paragraph is spot-on. So long as you have the physical space, it’s not a “now or never” thing. I went through my mother’s things in waves. Many items that were impossible to throw out the first time around had became less so when I revisited them a few months or a year later. It was a gradual process that felt reliable.

My sister and I evolved the concept of the “family archive”. So much that we as children were familiar with – such as what our parents looked like on holiday in their 40s – is fascinating to grandchildren who have only known them in old age, and the next generation will perhaps never have seen them at all.

articles.title: Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?
articles.summary: Experts share what you need to know about GLP-1-related hair loss as the side-effect gets more attention from researchers. About 20 million people across the US, UK, and EU are taking GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide (Ozempic or Mounjaro are common brands) for weight loss…
body: In one survey of people who take these medications, 20% of respondents experienced hair shedding, although the lack of high-quality data from a randomized, controlled trial to assess this side-effect makes it difficult to know exactly how common it is.

While GLP-1-related hair loss is often temporary and reversible, it’s significant enough that some patients hesitate to take drugs they would otherwise benefit from using. Here’s what you need to know.
Most people who take GLP-1 drugs don’t have hair loss. However, those who do often notice it within the first year, usually peaking a little before the 12th month.

articles.title: With turbulence all around, Armani plays it safe and easy in Milan
articles.summary: The late designer’s niece echoes his sense of relaxation, as the house seeks to prove itself to potential buyers. A year after the death of Giorgio Armani, the Italian fashion house he founded in 1975 is facing increasing uncertainty about its future ownership.
body: In his will, Armani, who ruled over the business for 50 years, instructed his heirs to sell an initial 15% stake of the company within 18 months of his death. If a private sale does not materialise, an IPO is mandated to take place. Now there are reports the group is readying itself for formal talks with the French conglomerate LVMH, the beauty giant L’Oréal and the eyewear group EssilorLuxottica – three of Armani’s preferred acquirers – over the possible sale of a minority stake.

Against this backdrop, pressure is mounting for the company to prove to potential buyers the continued allure of Armani. In 2025, its revenue fell for a second consecutive year, dropping 2.8% to €2.19bn.
In a turbulent luxury market, the question now is if Armani can remain a powerhouse without its founder – who turned it into an empire – at the helm.

So far during this era of upheaval, Armani’s niece Silvana Armani, who took over as creative director of womenswear after his death, has chosen to play it safe by leaning into continuity rather than any dramatic design shake-up.
points: The late designer’s niece echoes his sense of relaxation, as the house seeks to prove itself to potential buyers.

articles.title: Giambattista Valli Acquires Full Ownership of His Brand From Artémis
articles.summary: The Italian designer has acquired full ownership of his brand from the Pinault family’s holding company, with which he went into partnership in 2021.
body: Italian fashion designer Giambattista Valli has acquired full ownership of his brand from Artémis, the holding company of the Pinault family that controls Kering.

“We have been delighted to support Mr. Giambattista Valli and to stand behind such a singular and demanding creative vision. After years of an inspiring collaboration, a new chapter is now opening in this entrepreneurial adventure, and I wish Giambattista every success in the next stage of his journey,” François-Henri Pinault, chairman and CEO of Groupe Artémis, said in a statement. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The designer added that he would like to thank “Artémis for its support and commitment to the maison throughout all these years. This agreement now enables me to fully regain control of my brand and to pursue its development with enthusiasm and energy.”

In the same statement, the brand acknowledged that working with Artémis has helped to develop the brand’s infrastructure, scale its collections, and expand its international presence. Giambattista Valli has two standalone stores in Paris and Milan.
points: The Italian designer has acquired full ownership of his brand from the Pinault family’s holding company, with which he went into partnership in 2021.

articles.title: I Asked 5 Chefs Their Favorite 30-Minute Dinner
articles.summary: Every night we all ask (or get asked) one simple question: What’s for dinner? Whether you’re someone who likes to meal prep, plan your meals nightly, or just wing it, a tried-and-true recipe that you can whip up in no time is always a good thing to have on hand for busy weeknights.
body: Quick cooking doesn’t have to skimp on flavor. Here at The Kitchn, we’re big fans of meals that are ready in 30 minutes or less, especially if they can be made in just one pot. But what about the professionals? We were curious to learn their go-to recipes that are ready in half an hour and loaded with flavor. To find out, I spoke to five chefs. Surprisingly, there was one cut they all had in common: chicken thighs. Here are the recipes they always keep in their back pockets and how they like to zhush up this cut of meat.

Steve Ingber, executive chef and owner of MileHighCook, a private chef company in Denver, goes for chicken thighs on busy weeknights because they’re so forgiving. “My go-to is chicken thighs pounded thin, seared hard in cast iron, and finished with a quick pan sauce of garlic, lemon, butter, and whatever herbs I have,” Ingber says. “It’s on the table in 20 minutes. I cook for other people all week, so at home I want one pan and nothing fussy.” To ensure a consistent and quicker cook, “Pound the thighs to an even thickness,” he says. “They cook in six to eight minutes, and nothing dries out.”
points: Every night we all ask (or get asked) one simple question: What’s for dinner?

articles.title: Rooted in Reality: Key Takeaways From Milan Fashion Week Spring/Summer 2027
articles.summary: Milan Fashion Week provided a clever debut, some exciting new talent, and a clearer path for the city’s biggest brands this season.
body: Milan fizzed with excitement this season, from Gucci’s reconstructed store to Prada’s 63 skirts, a clever debut at Moschino, and a much-talked-about Vogue World; it was a week of creativity, celebrity, and online debate.

To the surprise of many, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni attended a gala on Wednesday night celebrating the opening of Milan Fashion Week and the new Dalí e la Moda exhibition, hosted by Camera della Moda Italiana and Milan Mayor Giuseppe Sala at the Palazzo Reale. Her attendance marked the first time in 10 years that a sitting Italian prime minister has attended Milan Fashion Week (the last time was Matteo Renzi in 2016). It also shows the Italian fashion industry is in a crucial turnaround period, as Milan, its brands, and its manufacturing networks try to return to growth (Italy’s annual fashion revenues have declined 8% since 2023, hitting €91.4 billion for 2026, per CNMI).

articles.title: She Painted Her Bedroom an Unexpected Color — It Created the Coziest Space
articles.summary: You might not always be allowed to paint the walls of a rental apartment, but if you are, it can make a huge difference in how the whole space looks. Plus, adding a just-for-you color to the walls can make your place truly feel like home.Take it from renter Juliana, who has a 600-square-foot…
body: In her bedroom especially, Juliana wanted a space that felt a little more homey. “I wanted to experiment with deep colors and textures to make the room feel cozy and complement the traditional wall trims and doors of the ’20s apartment,” she says.
Here’s how Juliana turned her blank canvas bedroom into a comfy retreat that’s packed with style.

Juliana decided to go for both color and texture, choosing a limewash treatment in a deep mossy green that felt “grounding and natural.” It was love at first sight when Juliana saw the paint online (it’s James Alexander’s Verde Terroso “Sage Green Limewash” ). “I was so invested in the color I didn’t even swatch it before ordering the paint. It was all or nothing on that color for me,” she says.

As for the process, Juliana took extra steps to make the walls look perfect. “I’m not usually one to prep before going for a project, but I knew that prepping the walls was an annoying step I couldn’t skip,” she says. “Limewash is a natural paint, and it won’t stick well over surfaces previously painted with your regular wall paint. I’m glad I followed the correct process for once because I absolutely love the result.”

articles.title: Coconut-Lime Sweet Potatoes
articles.summary: I haven’t always been the biggest fan of sweet potatoes –– I wouldn’t say I outright disliked them, but they weren’t my first choice. That is, until I found two cooking methods that really work for me: ultra-flavorful melting sweet potatoes, and the twice-baked technique used in this recipe.
body: Top crispy-tender, twice-baked sweet potatoes with a vibrant coconut-lime sauce, toasted coconut flakes, and fresh cilantro.

The sweet potatoes are mostly hands off –– unfortunately, you do still have to let them bake for a bit in the oven. However, I made up for that with crunchy coconut flakes that toast while the oven heats up and an easy, no-cook coconut lime sauce that gets into every sweet potato nook and cranny. The whole dish is salty, bright, and just the right amount of sweet to make a sweet potato lover out of anyone. Oh, and if you use the soy sauce and agave options, it’s also vegan, so truly something everyone can enjoy.

After going to culinary school, I worked all over the food space teaching cooking classes, leading projects at food non profits, developing recipes for meal kits, and even farming under the hot Texas sun. I’ve worked on hundreds of recipes over the past 10 years, making sure they look delicious and taste even better. I always keep the home cook in mind to ensure every recipe, from an easy weeknight win to a dinner party showstopper, is a keeper.

articles.title: Gianvito Rossi Marked 20 Years of Fabulous Footwear and a New Rizzoli Tome
articles.summary: For the brand’s 20th anniversary celebration at Palazzo Serbelloni during Milan Fashion Week, both Naomi Watts and Paloma Elsesser turned up in the Jessica—and told Vogue they were more than happy to spend the evening on their feet.
body: “I love the comfort and elegance,” said Watts, who styled her Jessicas with an Attersee pleated halter top and wide-leg trousers. “For me, elegance quickly fades if it’s not comfortable. Some people will suffer, but I don’t want to anymore.”

Elsesser, who also selected plexi Gianvito Rossis for her Vogue fall shopping guide, teamed her pair with a vintage Jean Paul Gaultier skirt and a leather bustier she thrifted in Paris. “There’s an admiration and a thought of the sensuality of women, but the need for comfort as well,” she said.

Rossi is deeply inspired by Umberto Boccioni’s Unique Forms of Continuity in Space, the Futurist sculpture of a figure striding forward, its body fragmented into aerodynamic forms that suggest speed and movement. The designer told Vogue that there are “two souls” to every collection, or perhaps that should be soles: one rooted in the house’s design language and another devoted to inventing new ideas that might eventually become signatures themselves. “There’s a part of the collection that is more about evolution, and there’s another part of the collection that is more about innovation,” he said.

articles.title: How to Get Empire State Building Tickets for Your Next Trip to NYC
articles.summary: Everything you need to know before visiting New York City’s most iconic skyscraper.
body: Ready to experience the Art Deco masterpiece yourself? Read on for everything you need to know before visiting the Empire State Building, including how to get tickets, what’s worth it, the best times to visit, and insider tips for how to make the most of your tourist dollars.

The Empire State Building is a 102-story Art Deco skyscraper located in Midtown Manhattan, designed by Shreve, Lamb & Harmon, and constructed swiftly between the years of 1930 and 1931 (that’s about 4.5 stories per week, making it one of the fastest large-scale construction projects in history). Standing at 1,454 feet tall, it held the title of the world’s tallest building for almost 40 years—that is, until the North Tower of the World Trade Center kicked it down the list in 1970. Today, it’s the eighth tallest building in New York City, and houses over 150 offices, most notably companies like LinkedIn, Workday, and Expedia.
